title: Margin-Learning Information Penalty for Principal Effects with Continuous Mediator and Binary Endpoint
banked_reason: Authoritative source-attested D0.5 FAIL: every-law canonical-information claim fails at permitted density-guard boundary laws; independent field gate gives incremental tier and paper-score ceiling 5.3 below 7.4. Managed validity audit confirms below-floor terminal; repair requires a new tangent/estimator program.
gap_reasons: The claimed unrestricted-margin canonical-gradient/information comparison is false at every stated P in P°: P° has Holder slack but no strict density-guard slack; e.g. f_min=1 permits f_zx≡1 only, so there are no nonzero two-sided margin paths in the asserted unrestricted model, while the displayed V_den can be positive for heterogeneous cell effects. Thus phi_np is not the canonical gradient and V_out+V_den is not its information bound at such laws.

The information theorem is false under its every-law quantifier: the permitted choice f_min=1 forces all normalized margins to be uniform, but two heterogeneous cells still produce V_den>0 although the unrestricted experiment has no margin-learning uncertainty. At those laws the named exponential-tilt family leaves the model, and Hölder-radius slack does not supply the missing density-bound slack; analogous tangent restrictions occur when densities contact their bounds on intervals. The mean-square expansion establishes the proposed estimator's variance coefficient, but that coefficient is not the canonical efficiency bound at these boundary laws, and feasible attainment of the known- and parametric-margin coefficients is not proved. The remaining delivered results constitute a narrow finite-cell estimator and matched one-dimensional rate benchmark, leaving the advertised attained information-cost characterization incomplete. [Zhang–Yang's public theorem text](https://arxiv.org/html/2406.13478v2#S3) already supplies the fixed-bandwidth gradients, and the author-defined support-relative regime establishes no improvement over their published admissible class. The central claim-fidelity defects, limited incremental scope beyond those gradients, and absence of an implemented numerical comparison constrain the projected paper score. [D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 5.3 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'subfield' is capped at 'incremental'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]

Complete a law-valid, feasible three-experiment information comparison, correcting boundary tangent spaces and proving known- and parametric-margin attainment alongside unrestricted-margin attainment.
proof_attempt_summary: Resumed the supervisor-approved OEQ repair, completed guarded-pilot and finite-fold proof closure, corrected the Zhang–Yang comparison to an explicitly paper-owned support-relative adaptation, and lawfully attested all three cited sources. Source-attested D0.5 refuted the every-law canonical-information claim at permitted density-guard boundaries; the invalid interpretation affects attainment, risk, homogeneous and comparator claims despite the preserved identification, path, pilot and rate arguments. A strict tangent-interior/active-boundary split and branch-correct known/parametric estimators require a new program; the independent gate rated this package incremental with ceiling 5.3 against the 7.4 field floor, so it was banked downgraded without formalization.
tldr: For a finite-cell randomized trial with a continuous mediator and binary endpoint, the common-law shrinking-bandwidth information comparison separates outcome information \(V_{\mathrm{out}}\) from the nonnegative margin-learning penalty \(V_{\mathrm{den}}\). The penalty vanishes exactly when the pointwise effects agree across positive-mass baseline cells. The guarded, foldwise-recomputed unrestricted-margin estimator has uniformly bounded pilot fourth moments and a mean-square negligible expansion remainder, and its empirical scaled-variance studentizer consistently estimates \(V_{\mathrm{np}}=V_{\mathrm{out}}+V_{\mathrm{den}}\). The main-model attainment and bias-aware inference results use bandwidth \(h\asymp n^{-1/5}\), with matched \(n^{-2/5}\) risk and honest-length orders. The separate support-relative Zhang--Yang comparison regime is an author-defined adaptation. Literal published ambient-S6 membership remains unavailable for these positive compact-support densities, and the published \(n^{-1/3}\) formula is only an upper-bound route.
gap: Published localized principal-effect theory gives fixed-bandwidth gradients and invokes an oracle EIF for its computational route, leaving both the common-law shrinking-bandwidth cost and attainment after unrestricted nonparametric margin estimation unresolved.
fill: The project starts from the explicit path \(f_{zx,\varepsilon}=f_{zx}(1+\varepsilon\ell_{zx})\), derives the direct and copula-CDF score coefficients with their correct normalizations, proves the regular-parametric contribution is \(O(1)\) in a named exponential-tilt experiment, obtains the exact heterogeneity penalty and its if-and-only-if zero criterion, and recomputes the unrestricted full score with guarded pilots whose target sup-norm rate is \(r_n=(\log n/n)^{2/5}\).
